name: Omniseo
summary: AI search visibility (GEO) tracking. Monitor and improve how your brand shows up in AI answers across ChatGPT, Google AI and other channels — track prompts, competitors and citations to grow AI-driven discovery.
best_for: brands and SEO teams that want to measure and improve how they show up in AI-generated answers (ChatGPT, Google AI and more) as AI search grows
skip_if: AI-driven traffic is still negligible for your business (classic SEO tools matter more), or you need concrete ranking control rather than visibility tracking
honest_knock: Two honest cautions. AI search visibility (GEO) is a young, fast-moving category. Tracking how you appear in ChatGPT and other AI answers is genuinely useful signal, but the metrics are far less standardized than classic SEO — and you're paying to monitor a moving target you only partly influence. And the step from Essentials to Professional is a big jump for more channels and prompts. Treat it as an early-mover intelligence tool, not a guaranteed ranking lever. Two smaller cautions from the pricing page itself, read on 20 October 2026. The trial covers two engines for seven days, so it cannot show you what the four- or ten-engine plans report. And support is email-only on both self-serve plans; chat and phone start at Enterprise. The crawler analysis the site promotes works from server logs and crawl events, and the pricing table does not say which plan includes it.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per month (4 AI channels, 50 prompts, 5 seats)
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-08-17, 2026-09-28 and again on 2026-10-20 against the vendor's own pricing page) Essentials $89/mo (4 AI channels, 50 prompts, 5 seats), Professional $349/mo (10 AI channels, 100 prompts), Enterprise from $899/mo with custom terms and volume. Annual billing is $890 and $3,490 a year respectively, which the page describes as two months free. There is a 7-day free trial with no credit card, after which the first paid month is half price — $45 instead of $89, or $175 instead of $349. The comparison table marks that first-month discount as not available on Enterprise.
